answer: Commit-and-reveal identity registration stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer posts a hash of its ID papers and device key and waits thirty days unpaid. Second, it reveals the papers for a public registry check, so one operator cannot mint a fleet. Third, a duplicate burns a $35 bond and blacklists the papers a year. Fourth, agents renew yearly. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real identities and $55,000 in bonds and fees, lost if caught. Trust is a jetty: honest boats wander in one by one, while a spiral of copies strands on the rocks, like a market where traders show ID first.
